meta.name: QQ Coffee · the site system
meta.title: One fluid size system for home, catalog and 25 coffee pages
meta.lede: The whole system of the new QQ Coffee site: 31 size roles drawn as lines from a 320 to a 1440 screen, three shared layout steps, one colour table, one motion vocabulary, the 3D packs. Everything was measured in a browser at every 10px of width and 25px of height; «before» is the Figma file, whose frames hold sizes as steps.
meta.footer: Measured in headless Chromium on the built site, 2026-10-19. Before = the Figma frames (320, 390, 768, 990, 1280, 1440, 1920); now = the site on branch site-system.

items.ask: Build the QQ Coffee website from the Figma file, hosted on GitHub
items.done: Static Vite site in timofeylebedev/qq, branch site-system; every push to main publishes to timofeylebedev.github.io/qq (deploy.yml; Pages source must be set to GitHub Actions once).

items.ask: Start with the main, catalog and product pages; other pages only as context
items.done: Home, catalog and one page per coffee (25), from one set of components. Not built: bag, checkout, search, favourites, account, other categories, journal, business pages (see Next).

items.ask: Figma is general inspiration, not exact values or structure
items.done: Sizes come from the site's own scale; structure follows Figma (sections, cells, hairlines, mono capitals). Where Figma differs between frames, the site takes one line through them: e.g. h2 32→48 where Figma has 32 / 36 / 40 / 48 steps.

items.ask: A fluid system, not breakpoints (exceptions allowed)
items.done: Every size is a straight line from its value at 320 to its value at 1440 (31 roles in design/scale.json), constant outside; the screen's height counts (a screen 360 tall gets the 320 sizes, 920 tall the 1440 sizes). Layout changes at only three shared column steps S 22rem, M 43rem, L 58rem, plus the navbar at 64em. Four exceptions use screen units on purpose, listed in decisions.json.

items.ask: A system within pages and between screen sizes
items.done: One ladder (steps 2/4/8/16), type levels ≥ ×1.125 apart at both ends, colours only from design/colors.json with contrast checks, one motion vocabulary; build/rules.mjs checks 9 rules on every build and in CI.

items.ask: Flow Medium's size system as inspiration
items.done: Taken from it: roles with two ends, the height-capped viewport (--vp), the ladder, relations, a decisions register, the rules check, the audit at 11 sizes, this report. Not taken: its modular ratio (QQ's Figma uses round values).

items.ask: Use the CSV, only rows «На сайте» = «Да»
items.done: 25 coffees from data/products.csv (Колумбия Вуш-Вуш appeared twice: the fuller row wins). Taste scores, descriptors, processing, lots, countries, tags and roast use reach the cards, filters and product tiles.
Placeholder prices per price group and weight in data/prices.json, marked as such (decision price-placeholder).
The Sumatra label on every pack, as you chose (decision pack-label).

Apercu Pro 400/500/700 self-hosted and subset; headings in JetBrains Mono Bold (Google has PT Mono only in Regular — decision font-headings); countdown digits in Technology Bold (your file, 1.2 KB subset).

items.ask: The pack moves in 3D on scroll
items.done: The pack is pinned under the navbar while five fact tiles scroll past and turns once around with them; it settles in from a quarter turn on load; still with «reduce motion».

items.ask: Packs on grey use the existing 3D model
items.done: One WebGL canvas per page draws every card's pack (your renderer as an ES module); cards lean with the scroll and turn to the pointer. A still of the same pack shows before WebGL draws and without it.
Waiting for the file or link; the footer shows the static logo meanwhile.
Figma frames measured into the size roles; this page is the full system report; the audit runs 4 pages × 11 sizes with axe and a 24px-text pass; an independent agent reviewed the work (Checks).

items.ask: Ask questions; report missing things later
items.done: Asked about repo, logo, labels, prices and fonts. Missing things are in Next.

blocks.title: Where the site departs from Figma, or does something you may not expect
items: Headings are JetBrains Mono, not PT Mono: narrower, with a different «Ж» and «Ш». A licence for PT Mono Bold swaps it in one line.
Sizes in between Figma frames are not Figma's: the site draws one line through each role, so e.g. the hero title is 55 at 1024 where Figma would show 56 (768 frame) or 64 (990 frame).
The countdown is 96 at 1440 and above, where Figma's 1920 frame has 128: nothing grows past 1440.
Figma's featured slide has a photo; the site shows the 3D pack unless data/site.json names a photo for that coffee.
On a phone sideways the hero is taller than the screen (555 px at 568 × 320): the title, the countdown and three links stack in one column below M.
The photos are Figma's moodboard, several with other roasters' packs: to replace before launch.

sections.title: The system
sections.sub: design/scale.json: one range (320 → 1440), one ladder, roles with two ends. build/tokens.mjs writes one clamp() per role and checks the rules.

blocks.title: The ladder
blocks.sub: Steps of 2 up to 24, of 4 up to 64, of 8 up to 128, of 16 up to 256. Every end of every role sits on it (dots).

blocks.title: Text roles
blocks.sub: Value at 320 and 1440 (constant outside), the face, where it is used, and the Figma steps at 320 / 768 / 1280 / 1440 / 1920 where one exists.
rows: section headings, the catalog tabs, the product's name on its page
headings of the image blocks (approach, about)
the name of the featured coffee
names on product cards, titles of tiles (business, info blocks, product facts), footer headings
eyebrows above headings («Наш подход»): set apart by colour and case, not size
the big sentence of a product's story
the caption over the featured photo, the text under a section heading
longer text: the featured description, the story columns, business text
card descriptions, lists, links of the navbar and the footer, fields
descriptor pills, captions above values in the buy bar, the copyright
big actions and values set in bold capitals: hero links, «В корзину», buy-bar values
prices and weights on cards (medium capitals)
the roast countdown in Technology Bold: a numeral display, the only size set by its figure, not its text

blocks.title: Levels that must stay apart
blocks.sub: The ratio of each pair at 320 (light) and at 1440 (dark). Two straight lines keep their ratio between its two end values, so the ends prove every size.

blocks.title: The height counts
blocks.sub: --vp = min(100vw, 2 × 100svh − 25rem): the width a screen counts as. 360 tall → the 320 sizes; 920 tall → the 1440 sizes.
blocks.note: The size a screen gets is the smaller of its width and this line.

from a section heading to its content

padding of big blocks: the featured text card, the text of image blocks, info blocks
padding of tiles: product facts, business descriptions, filter cells
height of the card's buy row and of big buttons
side padding of buttons and controls
padding above and below the cells of the hero
least height of the image blocks (approach, about)
width of the flame mark in the footer
the 3D pack on a product page: the side of its square (also capped by the screen's height)

blocks.title: Colours
blocks.sub: design/colors.json; text pairs checked for contrast on every build.

sections.title: The hero
sections.sub: The first screen of the home page: a drifting photo, the title, the countdown to the next roast, three links.

items.title: Height
items.html: min(100svh − 48, max(40vw + 14rem, 100svh − 7.5rem)): the screen less the navbar at most; on a tall screen it leaves 120px of the next block in view; never so short the photo vanishes (decision hero-height).

items.title: Cells
items.html: One column below M (stacked), two at M (title and countdown | links), three from L as in Figma. Cells are divided by hairlines; the links fill their cell.

items.title: Countdown
items.html: Technology Bold, --type-countdown 40 → 96, or 31% of its cell when the cell is narrower (decision countdown-fits-cell): 61 px at 768, 88 at 1280, 96 from 1440. Moscow time, weekdays at 10:00 (placeholder schedule).

blocks.title: The hero at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Peek: how much of the next block shows under the hero (negative: the hero is taller than the screen). Figma: the hero title of the nearest frame.

sections.title: The product stage and the buy bar
sections.sub: A coffee's page: the pack pinned while the fact tiles scroll past, the buy bar at the foot.

items.title: Pin
items.html: Height 100svh − navbar − buy bar (at least 22rem), pinned for as long as the five tiles take to pass; the tiles are 40% of the screen's height apart (28% from L), so scroll time is measured in screens (decision product-pin).

items.title: Pack
items.html: --stage 320 → 720, capped by the pin. It turns once around with qqStage.progress; tiles are frosted (cloud 70% + blur 40px) so the pack shows through them.

items.title: Buy bar
items.html: Two rows of cells below L (options; quantity, price, «В корзину»), one row from L as in Figma. New this round: on a screen under 32em tall it waits after the stage instead of following the screen, which pins at the whole screen under the navbar (decision short-screens).

blocks.title: The product stage at 25 screens
blocks.sub: Pin: the pinned height. Pack: the 3D box. Under bar: how much of the pack box the buy bar covers. Bar: its height and rows ("after": past the stage on a short screen).

sections.title: The catalog
sections.sub: Tabs, filters kept in the address, the grid.

items.title: Filters
items.html: Seven cells (sort, price of 200 g, type, line, country, processing, preparation) that wrap by width: 7 rows at 320, 4 at 375, 2 from 730, one row from 1260. A panel that would stick out on the right opens leftwards. The choice lives in the address, so a filtered catalog can be shared.

items.title: Grid
items.html: One column below M, two at M, and from L six tracks: the first four cards take half a row, the rest a third — the rhythm of the Figma catalog, kept only in the default order.

items.title: Tabs
items.html: «Все» and «Кофе» show the coffee; каскара, дрипы, сеты and мерч say they are coming (not in the shop yet).

blocks.title: The catalog at 25 screens
blocks.sub: First row: cards in the first row (the first four take half a row from M). Filters: rows of filter cells. First card: its top on the screen.

sections.title: The whole responsive picture
sections.sub: Every role and block size as the browser resolves it, every 10px of width (a screen 1100 tall) and every 25px of height (1440 wide). Dashed grey: the Figma steps, where a frame holds that size.

sections.title: Responsive map
sections.sub: What each block does at each width, from the sweep. Accent lines: the shared column steps (S, M, L land at these screen widths because the column is the screen less two gutters). Dashed: the navbar's page step.

items: S (22rem column) lands at about 380: it changes small things inside cards (the filter cells, the buy-bar captions), so it shows no row here.
Every block changes at the same two widths, about 750 and 1000; only the navbar has its own step (64em, so bigger browser text gets the burger sooner).
The catalog filter cells wrap by their own width (they flow), so their rows change at 370, 550, 730 and 1260 with no step.

sections.title: Motion
sections.sub: src/styles/base/motion.css: three curves and three times. With «reduce motion» every time is 0 and the packs stand still.

items.name: out
items.use: arriving and settling: hovers, panels, the toast coming in

items.name: pack follow
items.use: the packs follow their targets (scroll lean, pointer turn) at 9 per second

rows.name: product pack turn (one turn over 5 tiles)
rows.label: the scroll through the stage

items.title: In fast, out slow
items.html: Hovers come in at 0.2s and leave at 0.45s, so a pointer passing over a list leaves a soft trail (as Flow Medium).

items.title: One loop
items.html: The hero photo drifts 8% over 40s and back; it is the only thing that moves by itself, and it stops with «reduce motion».

sections.title: The grammar
sections.sub: How the site is drawn, in plain words, and which of these rules a script checks.

items.title: Colour
items.html: Ink #2d2f33 on paper, cloud #f6f6f6 for surfaces (cards, tiles, the buy bar), graphite and black for dark blocks, lavender for eyebrows and info icons. Secondary text is ink at 70%; 60% only for large text.

items.title: Type
items.html: Mono bold capitals tracked 0.05em for names and headings; Apercu for everything read; Technology digits for the countdown. Labels (eyebrows, controls, prices) differ by case and colour, not size.

items.title: Size
items.html: Every size a line from 320 to 1440 on one ladder; the screen's height counts; nothing grows past 1440, the column stops at 1520.

items.title: Shape
items.html: Sharp rectangles divided by hairlines; only pills and dots are round.

items.title: Layout
items.html: Everything sits in the content column; full-bleed blocks put their content in a column too, so they change at the same steps S, M, L.

items.title: Motion
items.html: Three curves, three times, one loop; the packs follow scroll and pointer.

blocks.title: Rules
rows: Sizes only from the scale; screen units only where a decision says
Layout steps only at S, M, L (and 64em, 25em, 32em tall)
No rounded corners except pills and dots
Type levels ≥ ×1.125 apart at both ends
Every row that scrolls sideways is position: relative
3D canvas at z-index 5; what shows above packs ≥ 6
Links inside the site through href(ctx, to)
One heading level per section; names in mono, text in Apercu
Cells inside a block share hairlines (margin −1px), never double lines

sections.sub: What was checked, how, and what is kept on purpose.

10 decisions, 3 exceptions, 8 placeholders

blocks.title: The rules (run on every build and in CI)

items.title: Colours only from tokens
items.how: no #hex, rgb() or hsl() in 13 stylesheets

items.title: Sizes only from the scale
items.how: font sizes are --type-* (or the 16px floor of fields, 12px of the counter); screen units only in 5 rules listed in decisions.json

items.title: Layout steps only at S, M, L
items.how: container queries at 22rem, 43rem, 58rem on the column; media only through media.css (--tablet 64em, --narrow 25em, --short 32em tall, input, motion)

items.title: Motion only from motion.css
items.how: transitions use var(--t-in/out/move) and var(--ease-out/move/leave); the hero's slow drift is the one loop

items.title: Faces only through tokens
items.how: font-family is var(--sans), var(--mono) or var(--digits)

items.title: The scale holds its own rules
items.how: both ends of 31 roles on the ladder, 9 type pairs ≥ ×1.125, 14 colour pairs

items.what: Headings and names are set in JetBrains Mono Bold (Google Fonts, self-hosted), not PT Mono Bold as in Figma
items.why: Google Fonts has PT Mono only in Regular; JetBrains Mono Bold was the closest of eleven Google monospace faces with Cyrillic in weight and shape (compared side by side)

items.what: The countdown digits are Technology Bold, subset to 0–9 and the colon (1.2 KB)
items.why: the font of the Figma hero; the file came from Tim

items.what: Every 3D pack shows the label of Индонезия Суматра Паллунг
items.why: only that label exists as art; products.json gives every coffee art: sumatra-front/back

items.what: Prices are placeholders by price group and weight (data/prices.json: Classic 250 / 680 / 2600 ₽ for 50 г / 200 г / 1 кг, Citric 290 / 780 / 2900, Special 390 / 1180 / 4400)
items.why: the price table has no prices

items.what: The photos are the Figma moodboard's: several show other roasters' packs (SIP, Cafe Public, Paloma, Stereoscope, MARU) and none is QQ's own; they are renders exported from Figma at 1280–1440 px
items.why: no other pictures yet

items.what: The hero shows a still of the Figma video (13456698-hd_1920_1080_30fps), drifting slowly, 1280 px wide
items.why: the video file is not in the Figma file's exports

items.what: The countdown and the catalog's shipping line assume roasting on weekdays at 10:00 Moscow time
items.why: Figma shows a countdown but no schedule

items.what: The sentences behind the plus of the three info blocks (roasting, payment, delivery) were written for the site
items.why: Figma has the plus but not the text

items.what: «В корзину» and the heart keep the bag and the favourites in the visitor's browser only (localStorage); there is no bag page, checkout, search, account or newsletter behind the site
items.why: these pages are not designed yet

items.what: Under 64em the sections open from the burger as a plain list
items.why: the menu is not designed

items.what: «Популярные» (the catalog's default order): coffees with a tag first, then Special, then the newest
items.why: no sales data

items.what: «Кофе с похожим вкусом»: the four coffees nearest in density, acidity, sweetness and ferment, nearer for each shared flavour family of descriptors and for the same line
items.why: the table has no explicit links between coffees

items.what: Secondary text is ink-70 (#2d2f33 at 70%), never ink-60 or ink-50 as some Figma texts are (the unchosen weight «1 кг», small numbers of the pager)
items.why: ink-60 is 3.8 : 1 on white and ink-50 2.9 : 1, below 4.5 : 1 for text; ink-60 stays only for large text (the inactive catalog tabs, 3 : 1) and parts of controls

items.what: No rounded corners: blocks, cards, buttons and fields are sharp; only pills (descriptors, the bag counter) and dots are round
items.why: the brand's grid of hairlines; Figma has no radius except pills

items.what: The navbar is 48px at every size, its links in --type-body
items.why: a control, not a block: as in every Figma frame

items.what: The hero is sized by the screen: 40vw + 14rem or the screen less 120px, whichever is more; at most the screen less 48px
items.why: a screen-sized block (the rule of the system: such blocks are capped by the height directly)

items.what: The product stage is pinned at the height of the screen less the navbar and the buy bar; the fact tiles are spaced by 40% of the screen's height (28% from L)
items.why: the pack turns as the tiles pass: the distance between them is scroll time, which is measured in screens

items.what: The countdown digits are --type-countdown, or 31% of their cell's width when the cell is narrower (cqi): eight digits are at most 2.7em wide, so they fill at most 85% of the cell
items.why: eight digits in a display face: the one size that has to fit a box, not a line

items.what: Four coffees show a photo on their card instead of the 3D pack (data/site.json photos), as the Figma catalog mixes them
items.why: the rhythm of the Figma catalog

items.what: On a narrow column the buy bar stays at the foot of the screen in two rows (options; quantity, price, button)
items.why: Figma has the bar only at 1440; buying should stay one tap away

items.what: On a screen under 32em tall (a phone sideways) the buy bar waits after the product stage instead of following the screen, and the stage pins at the whole screen under the navbar (no 22rem floor)
items.why: measured at 844 × 390: the two-row bar took 129 of 390px and covered the pack by 139px; a pinned block must fit the screen or not pin
